why: The name describes what the ranges do to travel and to plants alike, which is why so much grows there that grows nowhere else.

described: Of the Daxue. 大雪山 is great-snow-mountain, a high range in western Sichuan carrying permanent snow and ice above the forest.
traits: permanent snow and ice; a high range above forest; western Sichuan
name: great + snow + mountain
why: Three characters that each mean something and together say exactly what stands there.

described: Of Jiuzhaigou. 九寨沟 is nine-village-valley, a forested gorge holding a chain of lakes so clear the fallen trunks show on the bottom.
traits: a chain of very clear lakes in a forested gorge; nine villages along it
name: nine + village + valley
why: The Chinese name counts what was there and names the shape of the place, both of which read literally.

described: Of the Qilian, the long range walling the Gansu corridor from the Tibetan plateau, snow on its crest feeding the oases below it.
traits: a long range walling a corridor; snow on the crest; meltwater feeding oases below
name: wall + range
why: The range's name is Mongol for sky and is sounded out in Chinese. What it does, walling the corridor and watering it, is the fact about it.

described: Of Chengdu. 成都 is become-capital, the city on the flat wet plain of the Sichuan basin, mist over it most of the year.
traits: a city on a flat wet plain; mist most of the year; the Sichuan basin
name: made + capital
why: Two characters that both carry sense, naming what the place became.

described: Of Kunming, a city on a high plateau lake in Yunnan, mild the whole year round, too high to be hot and too far south to be cold.
traits: a high plateau lake; mild the whole year; neither hot nor cold
name: mild + high + lake
why: The Chinese sounds out an old tribal name. The even climate on a high lake is what the place is known for.

described: Of Lanzhou. 兰州 is orchid-region, a narrow city strung along the Yellow River between bare loess hills.
traits: a city strung along a river between bare loess hills; the orchid region
name: orchid + land
why: The Chinese name carries a plant in it and reads straight through.

described: Of Xi'an. 西安 is west-peace, the old capital at the eastern end of the road west, on a loess plain under the Qinling.
traits: the western peace; an old capital; a loess plain under a range; the head of the road west
name: west + peace
why: Both characters mean something and together say what the city was meant to be.

described: Of Chongqing. 重庆 is double-celebration, a city built on steep ridges where two rivers meet, fog standing in the valleys.
traits: built on steep ridges where two rivers meet; fog in the valleys; the double celebration
name: twice + joy
why: The name is two characters that both carry sense, which is the japonica move on a city.

described: Of Nanning. 南宁 is south-peace, a warm wet city on a river in the far south, green the whole year.
traits: the southern peace; warm and wet all year; a river city in the far south
name: south + peace
why: Named the same way as Annam to its south, by where it sits and what was wanted of it.

described: Of Guiyang. 贵阳 is noble-sun, a city on the Guizhou plateau where the sun is famously rare, cloud sitting over it most days.
traits: the noble sun; a plateau city where sun is rare; cloud most days
name: noble + sun
why: The name is ironic in practice and literal on the page, and the characters read directly.

described: Of Hangzhou, a city on a lake ringed by low wooded hills at the end of the great canal, tea growing on the slopes above it.
traits: a lake ringed by low wooded hills; the end of a great canal; tea on the slopes
name: lake + city
why: The Chinese sounds out an old name. The lake it is built around is what the place is and what it is visited for.

described: Of Sikkim, a small steep country on the southern face of the Himalaya where the land climbs from warm wet forest to permanent snow within a day's walk.
traits: warm wet forest climbing to permanent snow in one day's walk; the southern face of the Himalaya; very steep
name: steep + climb + land
why: The name is Limbu and opaque in Latin. The whole span from warm forest to snow in one slope is what the place is famous for.

described: Of Bhutan, a Himalayan country of deep forested valleys running south off the main range, wet on the southern flank and dry behind it.
traits: deep forested valleys running south off a range; wet in front, dry behind; the Himalaya
name: deep + forest + valley
why: The name is Sanskrit and disputed. The valleys running off the range, wet on one side and dry on the other, are the country.

described: Of Nepal, the middle of the Himalaya: the land rising in steps from hot lowland jungle through terraced hills to the highest snow on earth.
traits: rising in steps from hot lowland to the highest snow; terraced middle hills; the middle Himalaya
name: step + high + land
why: The name's origin is disputed and says nothing. Rising in steps from jungle to the highest snow is the fact about the country.

described: Of Assam, the broad hot valley of the Brahmaputra between hills, flooded every summer, the wettest country there is and the home of the tea bush.
traits: a broad hot river valley between hills; flooded every summer; the wettest country there is; home of tea
name: flood + valley
why: The name is Ahom and opaque. The flooded valley and its rain are what the place is.

described: Of Bengal, the great delta where two rivers come together and run out into the sea through a thousand channels, half of it water at any time of year.
traits: a great delta of a thousand channels; two rivers meeting; half water at any time
name: river + mouth + land
why: The name is a people's. The delta, which is the largest there is, is a fact about the ground.

described: Of Ceylon, a tear-shaped island off the south of India with a wet forested highland in its middle and a dry plain around it.
traits: a wet forested highland in the middle of a dry island; tear-shaped; off the south of India
name: wet + high + island
why: The old name descends through several languages from a word for the island itself. The wet highland in a dry island is what the place is.

described: Of Vietnam, a long narrow country curved down the coast, two river deltas at its ends and a spine of mountains between them, warm and wet the whole way.
traits: a long narrow curved coast; a delta at each end; mountains between; warm and wet
name: long + coast + land
why: 越南 is south-of-the-Yue, which names a people. The shape of the country, long and narrow between two deltas, is a fact about the ground.

described: Of Java, a long volcanic island whose spine is a line of cones, the ash making soil so rich it carries more people than almost any land its size.
traits: a line of volcanic cones down the spine; ash making very rich soil; densely settled
name: fire + mountain + island
why: The island is a row of volcanoes and the soil they made, which is what it is and why it is as it is.

described: Of Sumatra, a long island lying across the equator with a mountain wall down its western side and swamp forest spreading east from it to the sea.
traits: a mountain wall down one side; swamp forest spreading to the other coast; lying across the equator
name: wall + swamp + island
why: The name is local and opaque. The mountain wall on one flank and swamp on the other is the island's whole shape.

described: Of Dinghu. 鼎湖 is cauldron-lake, for the round steep-sided lake on the mountain that holds water the way a cooking pot does.
traits: a round steep-sided lake holding water like a pot; a forested mountain
name: pot + lake
why: Cauldron holds no root and would not earn one on four species. Pot is seated at three sounds and is the same vessel, so the name costs nothing and says the same shape.

described: Of Xinjiang, the new frontier, under an older spelling.
traits: the new frontier
name: new + border
why: The same province as xinjiangensis under an older romanisation. Two spellings of one place must reach one word or the language carries two.

described: Of Kashgar, the oasis ringed by desert, under a shorter spelling.
traits: an oasis ringed by desert; watered from the mountains
name: oasis + sand + land
why: The same city as kaschgarica. Romanisations differ and the place does not.

described: Of Songpan, the high pine country at the edge of the plateau.
traits: high pine country; grassland at the forest edge
name: pine + high + land
why: The same place as sungpanensis under a different spelling.

described: Of Dzungaria, the closed basin with no outlet.
traits: a closed basin with no outlet; sand and gravel steppe
name: closed + basin
why: The same basin as songorica, spelled with a doubled vowel.

described: Of Jinggangshan, the forested ridges with water-holding hollows.
traits: forested ridges with water-holding hollows
name: well + ridge + mountain
why: The same range as jinggangshanensis with the mountain word dropped from the epithet.

described: Of the Tumen, the cold shallow border river.
traits: a cold shallow border river; low wooded hills
name: border + river
why: The same river as tumenensis under a different spelling.

described: Of Dongeluo, a high valley on the Sichuan side of the Tibetan border, pine and rhododendron on the slopes above grazing ground.
traits: a high border valley; pine and rhododendron above grazing; the Sichuan side of Tibet
name: high + border + valley
why: The Chinese sounds out a Tibetan name, so the valley itself is described: high, on a border, wooded above the grazing.

described: Of the Hunan and Guangxi border country, a belt of low limestone hills between the lake plain to the north and the broad west to the south.
traits: low limestone hills on a border; between a lake plain and the broad west
name: border + stone + hill
why: 湘桂 is two province abbreviations joined, which names nothing. The limestone belt between them is the country the plants grow in.

described: Of Atuntze, a high town on the Yunnan side of the Tibetan border under a great snow range, the last settlement before the pass.
traits: a high town under a great snow range; the last before the pass; the Yunnan side of Tibet
name: snow + pass + town
why: The Chinese sounds out a Tibetan name. Where it stands, high and under snow at the head of a pass, is the fact about it.

described: Of Boluo, in Guangdong under Luofu mountain, a wet warm range of granite standing alone above the plain, long a place of hermits and temples.
traits: a granite range standing alone above a plain; wet and warm; hermits and temples on it
name: lone + mountain
why: The name sounds out an old one. A mountain standing by itself out of flat country is a shape anyone arriving sees.

described: Of Gulinqing, a narrow wet valley on the Yunnan border with Vietnam, forest reaching over the stream from both sides so the water runs in shade all day.
traits: a narrow wet valley; forest closing over the stream; the Vietnam border; shade all day
name: shade + stream + valley
why: 古林箐 names an old forest in a gully. The closed shaded valley is what the reserve is and why so much survives in it.

described: Of Maowen, a dry hot valley in the Sichuan mountains where the rain falls on the ranges either side and the floor stays parched, thorn scrub on the slopes.
traits: a dry hot valley floor between wet ranges; thorn scrub on the slopes; rain falls either side
name: dry + hot + valley
why: The dry valley in wet mountains is unusual and is exactly what makes the plants there different from their neighbours.

described: Of Luodian, a low hot basin in southern Guizhou where the limestone holds the heat and the winter never really arrives.
traits: a low hot limestone basin; heat held by the rock; almost no winter
name: hot + stone + basin
why: The name sounds out an old one. The heat trapped in a limestone basin is what grows the plants that are there.

described: Of Zhouqu, a steep narrow gorge in southern Gansu where the mountainsides are bare and loose and the river runs far below the settlements.
traits: a steep narrow gorge; bare loose mountainsides; the river far below
name: bare + steep + gorge
why: The Chinese sounds out a Tibetan name. The bare loose gorge is both the shape of the place and the reason it is dangerous.

described: Of Wuming, in the Guangxi karst where isolated limestone towers stand out of flat farmland, caves cut through their feet.
traits: isolated limestone towers out of flat farmland; caves cut through their feet
name: stone + tower + field
why: The towers rising straight from level fields are the whole landscape and are visible from any road.

described: Of Napo, on the Vietnamese border in Guangxi, limestone hills under monsoon forest, wet in summer and dry enough in winter to drop leaves.
traits: limestone hills under monsoon forest; wet summer, dry winter; a border county
name: border + stone + forest
why: 那坡 sounds out a Zhuang name. The seasonal forest on limestone is what the county is.

described: Of the Min, a river running out of the high mountains of northern Sichuan down onto the basin floor, grey with rock flour where it leaves the gorges.
traits: a river out of high mountains onto a basin floor; grey with rock flour; deep gorges above
name: mountain + river
why: 岷江 names the range and the river together. The river coming down off the mountains is the whole of it.

described: Laurel-family shrub or small tree of the warm south, leaves smooth and strongly aromatic when crushed, carrying its flowers singly or in twos in the leaf joints rather than in the usual cluster.
traits: flowers borne singly, not in clusters; strongly aromatic crushed leaf; laurel kin; warm south
name: alone + laurel
why: Lone holds no root and will not earn one on two species. Alone is seated at three sounds and says the same thing about a flower standing by itself.

described: Of Boluo, in Guangdong under Luofu mountain, a wet warm range of granite standing by itself above the plain, long a place of hermits and temples.
traits: a granite range standing by itself above a plain; wet and warm; hermits and temples on it
name: alone + mountain
why: Lone has no root. Alone is seated and a mountain standing alone out of flat country is the same picture.

described: Of southern China, the warm wet belt below the Nanling range where winter barely reaches and the forest stays green through it.
traits: the warm wet south of the middle land; winter barely reaches; evergreen forest
name: south + middle + land
why: Built on sinensis, which is already described as the middle land, with the south said plainly in front of it.

described: Of Shangri-La, a high plateau town in north-west Yunnan on open grazing land ringed by snow peaks, the old Zhongdian renamed for a book.
traits: a high plateau town; open grazing ringed by snow peaks; north-west Yunnan
name: high + meadow + town
why: The current name is borrowed from a novel and says nothing about the place. The high meadow ringed with snow is what is actually there.

described: Of the Caspian, the largest body of inland water there is, salt and falling, with no outlet to any sea and a shore below the level of the ocean.
traits: the largest inland water; salt; no outlet to any sea; shore below sea level
name: shut + salt + sea
why: The name is a people's. A salt sea with no way out, lying below the ocean, is a fact about the water.

described: Of Sogdiana, the old country between two great rivers in Central Asia: irrigated oasis cities strung along the trade road, desert between them.
traits: irrigated oasis cities between two rivers; desert between them; a road country
name: road + oasis + land
why: The name is a people's. What the country was, a chain of watered cities on a road through desert, is a fact about the ground.

described: Of Ninglang, a high county in north-west Yunnan holding a deep clear lake among pine-covered ridges, cold for its latitude.
traits: a deep clear lake among pine ridges; high and cold for its latitude; north-west Yunnan
name: deep + lake + pine
why: The Chinese sounds out a local name. The lake in the pines is what the county is and what anyone goes there for.

described: Of Pengshui, in the gorges of eastern Chongqing where the river has cut through limestone and the sides stand up sheer from the water.
traits: a river cut sheer through limestone; gorge walls straight from the water
name: sheer + gorge
why: The name sounds out an old one. The sheer-walled cut is the shape of the whole county.

described: Of Jiajin. 夹金山 is squeezed-gold mountain, a high snow pass in western Sichuan that has to be crossed to get from one valley system to the next.
traits: a high snow pass that must be crossed between valley systems; western Sichuan; the squeezed gold mountain
name: squeeze + gold + mountain
why: The Chinese name carries sense in both characters and reads straight through.

described: Of Penghu. 澎湖 is surging-lake, a scatter of low flat basalt islands in the strait, wind-scoured and nearly treeless, the sea loud on every side.
traits: low flat basalt islands in a strait; wind-scoured and nearly treeless; the sea loud on all sides
name: surge + lake
why: The Chinese name is the sound of the water around the islands and reads literally.

described: Of Lushi, a county in the Funiu mountains of western Henan, narrow valleys between wooded ridges with the Luo river running through.
traits: narrow valleys between wooded ridges; a river running through; western Henan
name: wood + ridge + valley
why: The county name carries a surname, so the valleys and wooded ridges are described instead.

described: Of Hong Kong. 香港 is fragrant-harbour, a deep sheltered anchorage among steep green islands, named for the incense wood once shipped out of it.
traits: a deep sheltered harbour among steep green islands; the fragrant harbour
name: scent + harbour
why: The Chinese name is two characters that both carry sense and together name the place by what it smelled of and what it was for.

described: Of Luofu, a wet warm granite range standing by itself above the Guangdong plain, long a retreat for hermits and the site of old temples.
traits: a granite range standing by itself above a plain; wet and warm; hermits and temples
name: alone + mountain
why: The same range as boluoensis, which sits at its foot, and a mountain standing out of flat country is what both names point at.

described: Of the Dabie. 大别山 is great-parting mountain, the range that separates the Yangtze country from the Huai plain, wooded on both flanks.
traits: the range that parts two river countries; wooded on both flanks; the great parting
name: great + part + range
why: The Chinese name says what the range does, which is divide one river's country from another's, and that is its whole significance.

described: Of Taiping. 太平山 is great-peace mountain, a high forested ridge in north-east Taiwan under almost permanent cloud, old cypress on its slopes.
traits: a high forested ridge under almost permanent cloud; old cypress; the great peace mountain
name: great + peace + mountain
why: Three characters that each carry sense and read straight through.

described: Of the Daba. 巴山 is the range walling the Sichuan basin from the north, deep wet valleys cut into its southern flank.
traits: the range walling a basin from the north; deep wet valleys on its southern flank
name: wall + north + range
why: The Chinese carries an old state's name, so the range is described by what it does: it shuts the basin off from the north.

described: Of Chengkou. 城口 is wall-mouth, a county at a gap in the Daba mountains where the only road through the range passes.
traits: a gap in a mountain wall; the only road through; the wall's mouth
name: wall + mouth
why: The Chinese name is a picture of the place: the opening in a mountain barrier that everything must pass through.

described: Of Tongjiang. 通江 is through-river, a county named for the water that runs clear through the limestone hills rather than around them.
traits: a river running through limestone hills; the through river
name: through + river
why: Both characters carry sense and together name the river's behaviour, which is what the county is called for.

described: Of Bawangling, a rainforest ridge in western Hainan, one of the last stands of lowland tropical forest on the island and the refuge of its rarest gibbon.
traits: a rainforest ridge; one of the last stands of lowland tropical forest; a refuge
name: last + forest + ridge
why: The Chinese names an old overlord. What the ridge is, the last of a forest that covered the island, is the fact worth carrying.

described: Of Diaoluoshan, a wet mountain in south-east Hainan where cloud sits on the forest most days and the streams run all year.
traits: cloud sitting on the forest most days; streams running all year; a wet mountain in Hainan
name: cloud + wet + mountain
why: The Chinese sounds out an old name. The permanent cloud and running water are what the mountain is and why its forest survives.

described: Of Musha. 霧社 is fog-village, a settlement high in the central mountains of Taiwan where cloud fills the valley for most of the morning.
traits: cloud filling the valley most mornings; high in the central mountains; the fog village
name: fog + village
why: The Japanese-era name is two characters that both mean something, and the fog is genuinely what the place is like.

described: Of Chatianshan. 插天山 is pierce-heaven mountain, a sharp ridge in northern Taiwan standing up out of cloud forest so steeply it looks driven into the sky.
traits: a sharp ridge standing out of cloud forest; so steep it looks driven upward; the sky-piercing mountain
name: pierce + sky + mountain
why: The Chinese name is a picture of the peak's shape seen from below and reads literally.

described: Of Dawushan. 大武山 is great-warrior mountain, the highest peak of southern Taiwan, standing alone above everything around it.
traits: the highest peak of southern Taiwan; standing alone above everything near it; the great warrior
name: great + alone + peak
why: The Chinese honours a warrior, so the peak is described by what it is: the high point standing clear of its neighbours.

described: Of Wugang, a county of low wooded hills and terraced valleys in south-western Hunan, wet and warm with bamboo on every slope.
traits: low wooded hills and terraced valleys; wet and warm; bamboo on every slope; south-west Hunan
name: bamboo + hill + valley
why: The Chinese carries an old military name. The bamboo hills are what the county looks like and what it lives on.

described: Of the Atlantic, the great ocean between the old world and the new, and of the coasts and mountains standing on its eastern shore where the weather comes off the water all year.
traits: the great ocean between two worlds; weather off the water all year; its eastern coasts and mountains
name: great + sea + coast
why: The name is a titan's. What the word points at is an ocean and the wet coasts facing it, which is a fact about the water.
